description: Critical-essentials NEVER-LIST: paths InterGen's AI can NEVER perform a destructive op on — no config option, ever. Everything NOT on this list is fair-game (per-capability user opt-in + per-action keystone consent). TEACHING CONTRACT (decided 2026-07-23): this list gates the AI's ACTIONS only — never the user's knowledge. When asked, the assistant states the block honestly (a code-level user-only boundary, never feigned incapability) and, on request, teaches the user how to perform the operation themselves, citing installed documentation, with safety context. Release-signed via OpenPGP (detached .asc), shipped to /usr/share/intergen/ — root-owned; its integrity rests on that signature, verified against the pinned release key before the manifest is trusted. dm-verity seals the live and install media only; the installed root filesystem is not a dm-verity device. Source-of-record: the 2026-05-30 critical-manifest design draft (internal records); prune+extension review decided 2026-07-23.

match_rules.prefix_semantics: a candidate path matches a prefix entry if, after expanduser()+resolve(), str(path) == prefix.rstrip('/') OR str(path).startswith(prefix)
match_rules.note: The signed manifest is the boundary; the per-action human modal is the net for any mis-categorization.

system_ai.description: InterGen's own machinery — the AI must never weaken, erase, or re-permission its own guards or evidence (anti-self-tamper). Includes the destructive-policy config itself (the linchpin: human-only) and the Sentinel/escalation/providers config (AI-immutable per Sentinel decision #5).
system_ai.notes: ~/.config/intergen/ covers dispatch-key, web-token, config.yml, the destructive-policy config, and the sentinel/escalation/providers config. /var/lib/intergen/ covers memory.db, governance + governance.sha256, mcp-pins, models, the consumed-nonce store, legal. /var/log/intergen/ is the carve-out from the otherwise-fair-game /var/log (anti-evidence-tamper).

boot_integrity.description: Boot + integrity chain — system won't boot / trust base broken.
boot_integrity.notes: /boot/ + /efi/ (ESP: bootloader, BOOT*.EFI, shim) + /etc/kernel/ cmdline.d + initramfs-generator config. Secure-Boot/MOK key material and the dm-verity roothash config live under these or under /usr (root-owned; block-read-only via dm-verity on the live/install media only). /etc/modprobe.d/ + /etc/sysctl.d/ added 2026-07-23: shipped kernel-hardening config (algif disable, dirty-frag mitigation) — removal = mitigation rollback.

identity_auth_privilege.description: Accounts, credentials, authentication stack, privilege-escalation rules, host identity.
identity_auth_privilege.notes: ssh_host_* = host identity keys (impersonation risk). sshd_config = remote-access policy. /etc/sudoers.d/ is also danger-equivalent to /etc/sudoers (a drop-in is identical in power).

package_supply_chain.description: Package manager DB + hooks + supply-chain trust root.
package_supply_chain.notes: /var/lib/igos/ = pkm DB (pkm.db), packages/ manifests, archives/, helpers/. /var/lib/pkm/ = pkm hooks (executable post-install -> code-exec risk if tampered) + repo metadata + available-updates.json. Distinct roles, both real. The intergenos-keyring trust root installs under root-owned /usr. /etc/pkm/ = repos.conf (which mirror pkm trusts) + trusted.gpg (the keyring the signed index verifies against) — the rogue-mirror/keyring-swap surface; added 2026-07-23.

filesystem_init.description: Filesystem + init essentials — system survival + identity.
filesystem_init.notes: /etc/systemd/system/ = system-critical unit overrides + default target (base units live under root-owned /usr/lib/systemd/system). Networking (resolv/hosts/nsswitch) + locale/vconsole/hostname KEEP per operator ruling. os-release = identity/version.

scheduled_task_persistence.description: Persistence vectors (round-3 hardening-review catch, EXTENDED 2026-07-23): any writable path that runs arbitrary code on a schedule, at login, or at dynamic link.
scheduled_task_persistence.notes: Distinct from the FAIR-GAME general /var/log decision. Binary dirs are covered by the system_binaries category as of 2026-08-16 (previously unlisted on the belief installed /usr was dm-verity read-only, which is true only of the live/install media). 2026-07-23 additions: shell-init (profile/bashrc/environment/profile.d) = code at every login, cron's sibling; ld.so.conf{,.d/} = library-path hijack at every dynamic link.

network_trust.description: Network security policy + TLS trust root (added 2026-07-23).
network_trust.notes: /etc/nftables.conf = the shipped default-deny firewall policy (intergenos-firewall-defaults) — "fixing" connectivity by weakening it is the never-class. /etc/ssl/ = CA trust store; one appended rogue CA is a silent system-wide MITM.

system_binaries.description: System binary and library directories (decided 2026-08-16): on an installed system these are root-owned but WRITABLE — dm-verity seals only the live/install media — so root ownership was their only barrier against a consented destructive action. No legitimate assistant flow destroys system binaries; recovery from a damaged /usr is a reinstall.
system_binaries.notes: The /bin, /sbin, /lib and /lib64 entries cover the FHS symlinks into /usr so a symlink spelling cannot route around the /usr entries (the matcher also resolves symlinks before matching — this is defense in depth, not the only guard). Package management remains unaffected: pkm runs outside the assistant's destructive-op gate.

dm_verity_readonly_reference.description: On the live and install media these paths are block-level read-only via dm-verity. On an INSTALLED system they are root-owned but writable — the manifest's enforcement teeth are for the writable criticals above, and root ownership is what protects these paths on an installed system.
dm_verity_readonly_reference.notes: Covers /usr/bin/intergen*, /usr/lib/intergen/** (incl. FDE/dm-verity boot tooling), /usr/share/intergen/models-manifest.json{,.asc} + this manifest, /usr/share/polkit-1/actions/org.intergenos.intergen.policy. The binary dirs (/usr/bin /usr/sbin /usr/lib and the /lib symlinks) carry their own never-list entries under system_binaries as of 2026-08-16.
